chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a male beggar comes to you at night, do not turn him away.'

key_terms.تَرُدُّوه: To turn away, to send back empty-handed; to reject a request
key_terms.سَائِل: One who asks/petitions; a beggar or one in need seeking help
key_terms.طَرَقَ: To come at night, to knock at one's door; to arrive unexpectedly

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about giving charity to beggars at night?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) commands believers not to turn away a male beggar who comes seeking help at night. This teaching, transmitted through the chain of Imams back to the Prophet, emphasizes that nighttime is a particularly vulnerable moment for the poor, and that charity must not be withheld merely because the request comes at an inconvenient hour. In early Islamic society, the night provided cover for the needy who were too embarrassed to beg in daylight, making this injunction especially significant.
word_analysis: comes to you (pl.) / knocks at your door
